C.1 Synthetic Dataset Construction Details
[id=A3.SS1.p1.1] To validate the model’s ability to extract hierarchical information from high-dimensional data, we construct a synthetic dataset generated from a common latent source. We employ a non-linear projection mechanism to derive task-relevant latent factors.
The data generation pipeline consists of three stages: source sampling, latent feature projection, and target/observation generation.
[id=A3.SS1.p2.1] Source Sampling.
We begin by sampling a high-dimensional source vector s∈ℝDt​o​t​a​ls\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{total}} from a standard normal distribution 𝒩⁡(0,I)\mathcal{N}(0,I). This vector contains all the primitive stochastic information of the system. We set Dt​o​t​a​l=13D_{total}=13.
[id=A3.SS1.p3.1] Latent Feature Projection.
To simulate the complex extraction of meaningful features from raw data, we map the source vector ss to a semantic latent space using a randomly initialized Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), referred to as the Encoder:
[id=A3.E14]
zb​a​s​e=MLPe​n​c​(s)z_{base}=\text{MLP}_{enc}(s)
(14)
[id=A3.SS1.p3.2] where zb​a​s​e∈ℝd1+d2z_{base}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{1}+d_{2}}. We then partition this feature vector into two distinct components:
[id=A3.I1.i1] 1.
[id=A3.I1.i1.p1.1] Dominant Factors (zd​o​m​i​n​a​n​tz_{dominant}): The first d1=3d_{1}=3 dimensions of zb​a​s​ez_{base}, representing high-level core features.
[id=A3.I1.i2] 2.
[id=A3.I1.i2.p1.1] Subtle Factors (zs​u​b​t​l​ez_{subtle}): The subsequent d2=5d_{2}=5 dimensions, representing fine-grained details.
[id=A3.SS1.p3.3] This projection ensures that the latent factors are non-linear transformations of the original source, creating a more challenging manifold learning task.
[id=A3.SS1.p4.1] Hierarchical Target Generation.
The regression target yy is derived from these projected factors using two separate random MLPs, fd​o​mf_{dom} and fs​u​bf_{sub}:
[id=A3.E15]
y=fd​o​m​(zd​o​m​i​n​a​n​t)+γ⋅fs​u​b​(zs​u​b​t​l​e)+0.15⋅ϵyy=f_{dom}(z_{dominant})+\gamma\cdot f_{sub}(z_{subtle})+0.15\cdot\epsilon_{y}
(15)
[id=A3.SS1.p4.2] We set γ=0.2\gamma=0.2 to scale down the contribution of subtle factors, making them harder to detect.
[id=A3.SS1.p5.1] Observation Entanglement.
The model observes a transformed version of the raw source vector ss. The input observation xx is generated via a linear mixing transformation of the source:
[id=A3.E16]
x=𝐖t​r​a​n​s⋅s+𝐛t​r​a​n​sx=\mathbf{W}_{trans}\cdot s+\mathbf{b}_{trans}
(16)
[id=A3.SS1.p5.2] where 𝐖t​r​a​n​s∈ℝDt​o​t​a​l×Dt​o​t​a​l\mathbf{W}_{trans}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{total}\times D_{total}} is a random matrix. This implies that xx contains all the information present in ss, but the semantic features zd​o​m​i​n​a​n​tz_{dominant} and zs​u​b​t​l​ez_{subtle} are implicit and must be recovered by inverting the relationship between xx and yy.
[id=A3.SS2]
C.2 Network Architectures
[id=A3.SS2.p1.1] Feature Backbones.
For tabular datasets (AEP, Concrete, Synthetic, Cement), we employ Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) with LeakyReLU activations. For the CIFAR-10 image dataset, we adopt a ResNet-18 backbone with the final fully-connected layer removed to extract latent features.
[id=A3.SS2.p2.1] Model-Specific Configurations.
[id=A3.I2.i1] •
[id=A3.I2.i1.p1.1] Ours. For tabular tasks, the encoders and predictors are MLPs with 2 hidden layers of sizes [100,100][100,100]. The discriminator is an MLP with 2 hidden layers of sizes [50,50][50,50], taking the concatenation of task and noise representations as input. To ensure training stability, we implement the adversarial component using the Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) framework, where the discriminator (critic) is updated nc​r​i​t​i​c=2n_{critic}=2 times per generator iteration. For CIFAR-10, the encoder utilizes the ResNet-18 backbone, while the remaining components follow the MLP-based design.
[id=A3.I2.i1.p2.1] To enhance training stability and representation diversity, we apply a stochastic weight perturbation strategy to the KL divergence terms. Instead of using fixed coefficients, we sample the penalty weight β\beta for each KL term from a normal distribution 𝒩⁡(μ,σ2)\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^{2}) for every training batch. This randomized scaling forces the model to adapt to varying regularization strengths. This process encourages the discovery of more robust and disentangled features. The specific μ\mu and σ\sigma values are determined based on the hyperparameter configurations for each dataset.
[id=A3.I2.i2] •
[id=A3.I2.i2.p1.1] MLP. We employ an MLP with 3 hidden layers of sizes [400,400,400][400,400,400] for these baselines. Since these models operate without a latent bottleneck, we adopt a shallower architecture. To ensure a fair comparison, we increase the hidden dimension to 400 to maintain a total parameter count consistent with the proposed method.
[id=A3.I2.i3] •
[id=A3.I2.i3.p1.1] ResNet-18. We adopt the ResNet-18 architecture as implemented in the InfoR-LSF repository.
[id=A3.I2.i4] •
[id=A3.I2.i4.p1.1] VIB. The encoder and predictors are MLPs with 3 hidden layers with hidden dimensions of [200,200,200][200,200,200]. The output dimension of encoder equals the sum of the dimensions of the two MLPs for zt​a​s​k1z^{1}_{task} and zt​a​s​k2z^{2}_{task}. This component maps the input to a dzd_{z}-dimensional latent space. For CIFAR-10, the encoder utilizes the ResNet-18 backbone, while the remaining components follow the MLP-based design.
[id=A3.I2.i5] •
[id=A3.I2.i5.p1.1] InfoR-LSF. We strictly follow the default architecture and hyperparameter settings from the official repository.

[id=A3.SS4]
C.4 Ablation Study Setup
[id=A3.SS4.p1.1] To verify the effectiveness of our proposed mechanisms, we design a comprehensive ablation study comparing four model variants and two training strategies.
[id=A3.SS4.p2.1] Model Variants.
We establish the proposed architecture as the baseline and systematically disable key components to isolate their contributions:
[id=A3.I3.i1] •
[id=A3.I3.i1.p1.1] A0 (Full Model): The complete AdverISF utilizing all three latent subspaces (zt​a​s​k1,zn​o​i​s​e1,zt​a​s​k2z^{1}_{task},z^{1}_{noise},z^{2}_{task}) with both variational inference and adversarial disentanglement enabled.
[id=A3.I3.i2] •
[id=A3.I3.i2.p1.1] A1 (w/o Multi-layer): To evaluate the benefit of the multi-layer separation architecture, we disable the second layer. The model is restricted to a shallow capacity, freezing the second layer’s parameters and generating predictions solely from the first level.
[id=A3.I3.i3] •
[id=A3.I3.i3.p1.1] A2 (w/o Variational): To test the impact of stochastic regularization, we remove the variational bottleneck. The reparameterization trick is disabled, and the KL divergence terms (β\beta) are omitted.
[id=A3.I3.i4] •
[id=A3.I3.i4.p1.1] A3 (w/o Adversarial): To assess the role of noise disentanglement, we remove the discriminator and the adversarial loss (γa​d​v\gamma_{adv}). The model is trained purely on reconstruction and variational objectives.
[id=A3.SS4.p3.1] Optimization Strategies.
We compare two training schedules to address stability in low-data settings:
[id=A3.I4.i1] 1.
[id=A3.I4.i1.p1.1] Joint Training: A standard end-to-end approach where all latent levels are optimized simultaneously.
[id=A3.I4.i2] 2.
[id=A3.I4.i2.p1.1] Two-Stage Training: A stepwise locking mechanism. In Phase 1 (initial 40% of epochs), the model optimizes the first level (zt​a​s​k1,zn​o​i​s​e1z^{1}_{task},z^{1}_{noise}) while freezing the second level (zt​a​s​k2z^{2}_{task}). In Phase 2, the first level is frozen to focus exclusive optimization on refining the deep latent features (zt​a​s​k2z^{2}_{task}).
[id=A3.SS4.p4.1] Hyperparameter Configurations.
To assess the individual contribution of each component, we employ a unified set of hyperparameters for the ablation analysis. The latent dimensions are fixed as d​i​m​(zt​a​s​k1)=4dim(z^{1}_{task})=4, d​i​m​(zn​o​i​s​e1)=8dim(z^{1}_{noise})=8, and d​i​m​(zt​a​s​k2)=5dim(z^{2}_{task})=5 across all variants. The specific regularization weights and discriminator iterations (nc​r​i​t​i​cn_{critic}) are configured as follows:
[id=A3.I5.i1] •
[id=A3.I5.i1.p1.1] Synthetic Dataset: The KL weights are βt​a​s​k1=0.2\beta^{1}_{task}=0.2, βn​o​i​s​e1=4.5×10−6\beta^{1}_{noise}=4.5\times 10^{-6}, and βt​a​s​k2=5.5×10−4\beta^{2}_{task}=5.5\times 10^{-4}. The adversarial training employs γa​d​v=0.11\gamma_{adv}=0.11 with nc​r​i​t​i​c=6n_{critic}=6.
[id=A3.I5.i2] •
[id=A3.I5.i2.p1.1] Concrete Dataset: The KL weights are βt​a​s​k1=0.035\beta^{1}_{task}=0.035, βn​o​i​s​e1=1.9×10−11\beta^{1}_{noise}=1.9\times 10^{-11}, and βt​a​s​k2=4.4×10−5\beta^{2}_{task}=4.4\times 10^{-5}. The adversarial training employs γa​d​v=0.17\gamma_{adv}=0.17 with nc​r​i​t​i​c=3n_{critic}=3.
